title: Kähler differentials of a polynomial ring are free on dx_1,...,dx_n
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ and $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring. Then the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{P/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a free $P$-module with basis $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$, and for every $g\in P$ one has $\mathrm dg=\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_k}\,\mathrm dx_k$, where $\partial/\partial x_k$ is the formal partial derivative of $P$ over $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, line 34306): Omega_{S/R} free with basis dx_1,...,dx_n for S = R[x_1,...,x_n]; the formula dg = sum (partial g/partial x_i) dx_i is the content of its proof (the R-derivations partial/partial x_i give the coordinates)
